name: Wellington
tagline: A compact, hilly capital wedged between harbour and wind-scoured hills, its café culture and film industry punching well above its small size.
highlight: A native bird calling from the bush at Zealandia at dusk, inside a predator-fenced sanctuary a ten-minute drive from Parliament.
shortDescription: New Zealand's compact, hilly capital, its café culture, film industry and predator-free wildlife sanctuary packed into a walkable harbour city.
metaDescription: A Wellington travel guide: Te Papa, the Cable Car, Zealandia, Weta Workshop, when to go and a practical two-day itinerary.
knownFor: Te Papa, the Cable Car, Weta Workshop, a strong café culture
goodFor: Museums, film history, an easy Cook Strait gateway

image.file: File:Lambton Harbour and the Wellington Waterfront.jpg
image.alt: Wellington's waterfront along Lambton Harbour, backed by hillside houses

intro: Wellington is one of the most compact national capitals anywhere, its city centre squeezed onto a narrow strip of flat land between a sheltered harbour and steep, wind-scoured hills — a geography that has kept the city walkable and dense rather than sprawling, even as it grew into New Zealand's political and cultural centre.

That compactness has produced an outsized café and arts culture for a city this size: Wellington regularly claims some of the best coffee anywhere in the world, and Peter Jackson's Weta Workshop turned the city into a real centre of the global film industry, its effects and props work visible in Wellington Airport's own Lord of the Rings-themed displays.

Wellington is also serious about conservation — Zealandia, a predator-fenced valley reserve barely ten minutes from Parliament, has helped native bird populations recover within city limits in a way few other capitals anywhere can claim.

whyVisit.intro: Wellington's case is a compact, walkable capital with outsized museums, café culture and film history for its size.

points.title: Te Papa is one of the world's best national museums
points.text: Free entry and an engaging mix of Maori taonga, natural history and interactive exhibits make it easy to lose half a day here.

points.title: The café culture is world class
points.text: Wellington regularly ranks among the best coffee cities anywhere, a real point of local pride rather than marketing.

points.title: Weta Workshop makes the film history tangible
points.text: Peter Jackson's effects studio turned Wellington into a real global film hub, and workshop tours show the actual craft behind it.

points.title: Zealandia is unlike anything in most other capitals
points.text: A predator-fenced valley reserve minutes from Parliament has helped native bird species recover within the city itself.

points.title: It's walkable and compact
points.text: Most of the city's key sights sit within an easy walk of each other, a real contrast to more sprawling capitals.

attractionsIntro: Wellington's essential sights fit within a compact, walkable harbourside centre.

attractions.name: Te Papa Tongarewa

image.file: File:Wellington pirogues du Musée Te Papa Tongarewa (2).jpg
image.alt: A traditional Maori waka (canoe) on display at Te Papa Tongarewa museum

attractions.text: New Zealand's national museum, free to enter, its collection spanning Maori taonga (treasures), natural history and interactive exhibits across six floors.
attractions.tip: Allow at least half a day — the museum is larger and more absorbing than its compact exterior suggests.

attractions.name: The Wellington Cable Car

image.alt: The Wellington Cable Car climbing toward the Botanic Garden

attractions.text: A historic funicular railway climbing from the city centre to Kelburn, its upper station offering sweeping harbour views and direct access to the Botanic Garden.
attractions.tip: Ride up and walk back down through the Botanic Garden — a pleasant, mostly downhill route back to the centre.

attractions.name: Wellington Botanic Garden

image.file: File:Joy Fountain, Wellington Botanic Garden, New Zealand.jpg
image.alt: The Joy Fountain in Wellington's Botanic Garden

attractions.text: A well-kept hillside garden connecting the Cable Car's upper station to the city centre, with themed plantings and sweeping views along the way down.
attractions.tip: The rose garden and duck pond near the bottom are a pleasant final stretch before re-entering the city.

attractions.name: The Beehive and Parliament

image.file: File:Beehive and Parliament House - Wellington - New Zealand - DSC00165.jpg
image.alt: The distinctive rounded Beehive building beside Parliament House in Wellington

attractions.text: New Zealand's distinctive executive wing, its rounded 'Beehive' shape a real architectural landmark beside the more traditional Parliament House and Library.
attractions.tip: Free guided tours of Parliament run regularly — a worthwhile look at how the country's government actually works.

attractions.name: Zealandia

image.file: File:Water - Zealandia (Karori Wildlife Sanctuary) - Wellington - New Zealand - DSC00196.jpg
image.alt: The forested valley reservoir inside Zealandia wildlife sanctuary

attractions.text: A pioneering predator-fenced valley reserve, its native bird and reptile populations recovering within a ten-minute drive of Parliament, unlike almost anywhere else this close to a capital city.
attractions.tip: A daytime visit shows the landscape and some birdlife; a guided night tour is the best way to spot kiwi.

attractions.name: Cuba Street

image.alt: The pedestrianised, colourful storefronts of Cuba Street in Wellington

attractions.text: Wellington's bohemian pedestrian strip, lined with independent cafés, vintage shops and street art, a real showcase of the city's creative character.
attractions.tip: The Bucket Fountain is a beloved, slightly odd local landmark near the street's northern end — worth a quick look.

attractions.name: Mount Victoria lookout

image.alt: Wellington's harbour and city seen from the Mount Victoria lookout

attractions.text: A sweeping viewpoint over the harbour, city and surrounding hills, reachable by a short drive or a steeper walk from the city centre.
attractions.tip: Sunset here is spectacular, with the harbour catching the last light below the city skyline.

thingsToDoIntro: Wellington's compact size and creative culture reward unhurried exploration on foot.

thingsToDo.title: Ride the Cable Car and walk down through the Botanic Garden

image.alt: The Wellington Cable Car, with views over the city and harbour

thingsToDo.text: A classic Wellington half-day: ride up for the views, then take a leisurely downhill walk back through the Botanic Garden.
thingsToDo.tip: The full walk down takes about 30–45 minutes at an unhurried pace, with several places to stop along the way.

thingsToDo.title: Tour Weta Workshop

image.alt: Weta Workshop, the film effects studio behind The Lord of the Rings

thingsToDo.text: Guided tours show the practical effects, prop-making and creature design behind The Lord of the Rings, The Hobbit and numerous other major films.
thingsToDo.tip: Book tours online ahead — sessions are limited in size and popular time slots sell out.

thingsToDo.title: Explore Cuba Street's cafés and bars

image.alt: Cafés and independent shops along Wellington's Cuba Street

thingsToDo.text: The best single stretch to experience Wellington's celebrated café culture and creative, independent retail scene.
thingsToDo.tip: Wellington's coffee reputation is earned — try a flat white at more than one café to compare.

thingsToDo.title: Walk the waterfront

image.file: File:Lambton Harbour and the Wellington Waterfront.jpg
image.alt: Wellington's waterfront promenade along Lambton Harbour

thingsToDo.text: A pleasant, flat promenade connects the city centre to Oriental Bay, passing public art, swimming spots and waterfront bars along the way.
thingsToDo.tip: Continue as far as Oriental Bay for a good beach-side lunch spot with harbour views.

thingsToDo.title: Spot native wildlife on a Zealandia night tour

image.file: File:Water - Zealandia (Karori Wildlife Sanctuary) - Wellington - New Zealand - DSC00196.jpg
image.alt: The forest valley inside Zealandia, home to native New Zealand wildlife

thingsToDo.text: A guided evening tour offers one of the more reliable chances to spot a wild kiwi anywhere in the country, alongside other native nocturnal species.
thingsToDo.tip: Book well ahead — night tours are popular and run with limited group sizes.

thingsToDo.title: Day-trip to the Wairarapa wine region
thingsToDo.text: Martinborough and the wider Wairarapa, a well-regarded pinot noir wine region, sit about an hour's drive or train ride from Wellington.
thingsToDo.tip: The Wairarapa Wine Train runs seasonally from Wellington — a relaxed way to visit without driving.

foodIntro: Wellington's food and drink culture is built around its café scene, alongside the usual excellent New Zealand classics.

foods.name: Flat white

image.file: File:Flat white coffee Highgate Cricket Club, Crouch End, London 01.jpg
image.alt: A flat white coffee, central to Wellington's celebrated café culture

foods.text: Wellington's café scene treats the flat white as a serious craft, regularly ranking among the best coffee cities in the world for its density of quality independent roasters.
foods.whereToTry: Independent cafés throughout Cuba Street and the wider city centre.

foods.name: Craft beer
foods.text: Wellington has one of New Zealand's strongest craft beer scenes, with numerous small breweries and dedicated tap rooms across the city.
foods.whereToTry: Craft beer bars around Courtenay Place and the wider city centre.

foods.name: Fish and chips

image.alt: A classic New Zealand fish and chips takeaway

foods.text: A beloved national tradition, best eaten from the paper along the waterfront at Oriental Bay.
foods.whereToTry: Independent fish and chip shops around the waterfront and Oriental Bay.

foods.name: Meat pie

image.file: File:Steak and cheese pie - Napier, New Zealand.jpg
image.alt: A classic New Zealand meat pie

foods.text: A serious national obsession — flaky pastry filled with steak, mince or other fillings, sold at bakeries citywide.
foods.whereToTry: Independent bakeries throughout the city centre.

foods.name: Pavlova

image.alt: A pavlova dessert topped with cream and fresh fruit

foods.text: A meringue-based dessert with a crisp shell and marshmallow centre, a beloved national favourite found on café menus citywide.
foods.whereToTry: Cafés throughout the city centre, especially at weekend brunch spots.

foods.name: Green-lipped mussels

image.alt: Green-lipped mussels, a New Zealand seafood specialty

foods.text: A distinctive New Zealand species, widely available on Wellington restaurant menus, served simply steamed or in a range of sauces.
foods.whereToTry: Seafood restaurants around the waterfront and Courtenay Place.

accommodation.intro: Wellington is compact enough that the city centre works as a base for almost any visit.

areas.name: City centre and Lambton Quay
areas.bestFor: Walking distance to Te Papa and the waterfront
areas.text: The most convenient base for sightseeing, close to the Cable Car, Parliament and the museum.

areas.name: Cuba Street and Te Aro
areas.text: A short walk from the centre, the best base for visitors prioritising Wellington's dining and bar scene.

areas.name: Oriental Bay
areas.text: A pleasant beachside neighbourhood a short walk or bus ride from the city centre.

gettingThere.intro: Wellington sits at the genuine crossing point between the North and South Islands, with an airport, ferry terminal and rail links.

options.text: Regular flights connect Wellington to [[auckland|Auckland]], [[christchurch|Christchurch]] and [[queenstown|Queenstown]] efficiently.
options.detail: Wellington Airport's short runway, exposed to strong local winds, is a well-known point of local pride and occasional traveller nerves.

options.text: Connects Wellington to Picton across Cook Strait, a scenic crossing through the Marlborough Sounds.
options.detail: Book vehicle space well ahead in summer — sailings can sell out.

options.text: The Capital Connection and other regional services connect Wellington to nearby towns including the Wairarapa.
options.detail: A relaxed way to reach day-trip destinations without driving.

gettingAround.intro: Wellington's city centre is compact and walkable, with the Cable Car and buses covering the hillier areas.

options.text: Te Papa, the waterfront and Cuba Street are all within a compact, flat central area.
options.detail: Some neighbourhoods climb steep hills — comfortable shoes help.

options.text: The Cable Car reaches the Botanic Garden and Kelburn, while a citywide bus network covers everywhere else.
options.detail: A Snapper card covers bus fares — tap on and off for each journey.

options.text: Useful for day trips to the Wairarapa or Kapiti Coast, though unnecessary for the city itself.
options.detail: Wellington's steep, narrow streets make a car more hassle than help within the city centre.

bestTime.headline: December–March for the mildest, least windy weather
bestTime.summary: Wellington is famous for its wind in any season, though summer offers the calmest, most reliable conditions.

seasons.text: The warmest, calmest weather, ideal for the waterfront and outdoor café culture.
Mild and settled, with noticeably thinner crowds than summer.
Cold and windy, though museums and indoor sights work well regardless of weather.
Increasingly mild, though still prone to the city's famous wind.

bestTime.avoid: Nothing strongly, though Wellington's wind is a year-round feature of the city rather than confined to one season — pack accordingly.

itinerary.title: Two days in Wellington
itinerary.intro: Built around the city centre's museums and a wildlife-focused evening.

days.title: Te Papa and the Cable Car
days.afternoon: The Cable Car up to Kelburn and a walk back through the Botanic Garden.
days.evening: Dinner and drinks on Cuba Street.

days.title: Film history and wildlife
days.summary: Weta Workshop and a genuine wildlife encounter.
days.afternoon: The waterfront walk to Oriental Bay.
days.evening: A Zealandia night tour to spot native wildlife.

tipsIntro: Practical notes on booking, timing and transport that make a real difference to a Wellington trip.
tips: Book Weta Workshop tours and Zealandia night tours online ahead — both are popular and limited in size.
Pack a windproof layer regardless of season — Wellington's wind is a year-round feature of the city.
Book Interislander ferry vehicle space well ahead in summer if driving across Cook Strait.
Allow at least half a day for Te Papa — it's larger and more absorbing than it first appears.
Try coffee at more than one Cuba Street café — Wellington's reputation for it is well earned.
Combine Wellington with a day trip to the Wairarapa wine region if you have an extra day to spare.

faq.q: How many days do you need in Wellington?
faq.a: Two days covers Te Papa, the Cable Car and Weta Workshop comfortably, with time for a Zealandia night tour and a walk along the waterfront.
Yes — it offers a free, world-class national museum, an outsized café and arts culture for its size, and a pioneering wildlife sanctuary minutes from Parliament.

A predator-fenced valley wildlife reserve barely ten minutes from central Wellington, where native bird and reptile populations have recovered within city limits — a night tour offers one of the more reliable chances to spot a wild kiwi.
Yes, famously so, in any season — pack a windproof layer regardless of when you visit, since it's a real year-round feature of the city rather than confined to winter.

faq.q: Can you visit Weta Workshop without booking ahead?
faq.a: It's risky not to — guided tours run in limited group sizes and popular time slots regularly sell out, especially in summer.

faq.q: How do you get from Wellington to the South Island?
faq.a: The Interislander ferry crosses Cook Strait to Picton in a scenic journey through the Marlborough Sounds, or a domestic flight connects Wellington to Christchurch or Queenstown quickly.
